quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #22
										  					
  

40 Questions • Passing Score 32

questions.question: When changing lanes, you should never:

options.text: Look over your shoulder to check your blind spot.
Change lanes suddenly or without warning.
Check for other vehicles moving into the same lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes suddenly or without warning.
questions.explanation: Before changing lanes, check your mirrors and blind spots to make sure no vehicles are in the space you want to enter. Always signal before changing lanes. This gives other drivers time to react.

questions.question: You want to park uphill on a two-way road with no curb. Which way should you turn your front wheels?

options.text: Straight ahead
Right, toward the side of the road
Left, toward the center of the road

questions.correctAnswerText: Right, toward the side of the road
questions.explanation: When parking uphill or downhill on a road with no curb, turn your wheels away from traffic. This way, if your brakes fail, the vehicle will roll away from the center of the road.

questions.question: A large truck ahead of you is turning right onto a street with two lanes in each direction. The truck:

options.text: May complete its turn in either of the two lanes.
May have to swing wide to complete the right turn.
Must stay in the right lane at all times while turning.

questions.correctAnswerText: May have to swing wide to complete the right turn.
questions.explanation: When turning, the rear wheels of a vehicle follow a shorter path than the front wheels. Long trucks need more space to turn. They often must swing wide to complete a right turn safely.

questions.question: Which one is a safe driving technique?

options.text: Using your high beam lights in fog.
Staring at the road directly ahead.
Checking your rearview mirrors often.

questions.correctAnswerText: Checking your rearview mirrors often.
questions.explanation: Check your mirrors every 2 to 5 seconds to be aware of hazards. Do not stare only at the road ahead. In fog, use low beam headlights, not high beams. Avoid looking directly at oncoming headlights to prevent glare blindness.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: Side road.
Merge.
Yield the right-of-way.

questions.correctAnswerText: Side road.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that a side road is ahead at an intersection.

questions.question: Drivers turning left must yield to:

options.text: Oncoming vehicles traveling straight or turning right.
Passing cars.
No one in particular.

questions.correctAnswerText: Oncoming vehicles traveling straight or turning right.
questions.explanation: When making a left turn, yield to all vehicles coming from the opposite direction. This includes cars, bicycles, and motorcycles.

questions.question: Which of the following is most likely to be slippery after snow or rain in cold weather?

options.text: A hilly, open road
A residential road
A road in a shaded area

questions.correctAnswerText: A road in a shaded area
questions.explanation: Shaded areas freeze before other parts of the road and thaw out later. On cold, wet days, these shaded spots become icy first.

questions.question: The speed limit on a country paved road is 45 mph unless otherwise posted.

options.text: 20 mph.
30 mph.
45 mph.

questions.correctAnswerText: 45 mph.
questions.explanation: The speed limit on a country paved road is 45 miles per hour. Always follow posted speed limits if they are different.

questions.question: This sign means you are approaching a railroad crossing with no signal. You should:

options.text: Come to a complete stop.
Keep a steady speed while looking and listening for trains.
Slow down, look both ways, listen for trains, and be ready to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down, look both ways, listen for trains, and be ready to stop.
questions.explanation: At a railroad crossing with this sign, slow down and check both directions for trains. Listen carefully and be prepared to stop. Never try to outrun a train.

questions.question: You have enough space to return to the driving lane after passing when:

options.text: The other driver signals for you to re-enter the lane.
You look over your shoulder and see the passed car behind you.
You can see both headlights of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can see both headlights of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.
questions.explanation: When you can see both headlights of the vehicle you passed in your rearview mirror, there is a safe gap between you. It is then safe to return to the driving lane.

questions.question: When driving at night, you should:

options.text: Always use your high beams.
Look directly at the headlights of oncoming vehicles.
Increase your following distance.

questions.correctAnswerText: Increase your following distance.
questions.explanation: Increase your distance between vehicles when it is dark and hard to see. Use your headlights properly. Do not look directly at oncoming headlights because the glare can blind you.

questions.question: When should your wheels NOT be pointed straight ahead?

options.text: When waiting to make a left turn at a traffic light.
When parked on a hill or sloping driveway.
When parked on the side of a level roadway with no curb.

questions.correctAnswerText: When parked on a hill or sloping driveway.
questions.explanation: When waiting to turn left, keep wheels straight. If hit from behind, this prevents you from moving into oncoming traffic. When parked on a hill, angle your wheels so the vehicle rolls away from traffic if brakes fail.

questions.question: Which factor affects how quickly a person absorbs alcohol?

options.text: Weight
Height
Intelligence

questions.correctAnswerText: Weight
questions.explanation: Body weight affects alcohol absorption. Other factors include biological sex and how much food is in your stomach. The only way to remove alcohol from your system is to wait.

questions.question: If you park facing uphill on a curbed street, set the parking brake and:

options.text: Turn the front wheels toward the curb.
Turn the front wheels away from the curb.
Leave the front wheels straight.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn the front wheels away from the curb.
questions.explanation: When parking uphill on a street with a curb, turn wheels away from the curb. When parking uphill without a curb or downhill with a curb, turn wheels toward the curb or road edge.

questions.question: This road sign means:

options.text: Do not enter.
No parking.
No U-turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: No U-turn.
questions.explanation: This sign means you cannot make a U-turn. You cannot turn around to go in the opposite direction at this location.

questions.question: When a school bus is picking up or dropping off children, you must:

options.text: Stop, regardless of your direction of travel.
Stop if you are traveling in the same direction.
Slow down and be prepared to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop, regardless of your direction of travel.
questions.explanation: When you see a school bus picking up or dropping off children, you must come to a complete stop before you reach the bus. This applies no matter which direction you are traveling.

questions.question: You reach a four-way stop at the same time as the driver on your left. Who has the right-of-way?

options.text: The driver on your left has the right-of-way.
You have the right-of-way.
Whoever is signaling to make a turn has the right-of-way.

questions.correctAnswerText: You have the right-of-way.
questions.explanation: When two vehicles arrive at a four-way stop at the same time, the vehicle to the right has the right-of-way.

questions.question: You are approaching an intersection with a steady yellow light and have not entered yet. You should:

options.text: Speed up to beat the red light.
Reduce your speed and proceed carefully through the intersection.
Come to a safe stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Come to a safe stop.
questions.explanation: When you see a steady yellow light, prepare to stop. If you are already in the intersection, clear it as quickly as possible.

questions.question: The first thing alcohol affects is:

options.text: Vision.
Judgment.
Balance.

questions.correctAnswerText: Judgment.
questions.explanation: Alcohol affects your brain's judgment first. It reduces all your safe driving abilities. Alcohol travels from your stomach to your blood and then to other parts of your body.

questions.question: It is legal to turn left at a red light after stopping only if:

options.text: You are on a two-way street turning onto a two-way street.
You are on a one-way street turning onto another one-way street.
You yield to all other traffic at the intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: You are on a one-way street turning onto another one-way street.
questions.explanation: After a complete stop, you may turn left at a red light only if you are on a one-way street turning onto another one-way street. No signs can prohibit the turn.

questions.question: If another driver is passing you in a no passing zone, what should you do?

options.text: Pull off the road.
Keep your speed and position the same.
Slow down and let the other driver safely return to your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and let the other driver safely return to your lane.
questions.explanation: Help the passing vehicle return to your lane safely and easily. This keeps everyone safe from hazards ahead.

questions.question: When are roads most slippery?

options.text: When it has been raining hard for several hours.
When they are clean and dry.
Just after rain starts.

questions.correctAnswerText: Just after rain starts.
questions.explanation: Roads are most slippery when rain first starts. Water mixes with oil and chemicals on the road that have not yet washed away. Be extra careful during the first rain.

questions.question: A driver license is a:

options.text: Right, not a privilege.
Privilege, not a right.
Requirement.

questions.correctAnswerText: Privilege, not a right.
questions.explanation: A driver license is a privilege. You must earn it and keep it.

questions.question: Why is it dangerous to follow a motorcycle too closely?

options.text: They do not follow the same rules as other vehicles.
Motorcycles can stop much faster than regular vehicles.
They brake more slowly than regular vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Motorcycles can stop much faster than regular vehicles.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles can stop very quickly. Following too closely gives you no time to react if the motorcycle stops suddenly. You need space to avoid a crash.

questions.question: When driving in fog, you should:

options.text: Slow down and use low beam headlights.
Slow down and use high beam headlights.
Turn your lights on and off to warn other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and use low beam headlights.
questions.explanation: Slow down and use low beam headlights in fog. If you cannot see ahead, pull off the road and wait for the fog to clear.

questions.question: If oncoming headlights are blinding you at night, what should you do?

options.text: Look toward the right edge of the road.
Switch your lights to high beams.
Turn your lights on and off.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look toward the right edge of the road.
questions.explanation: Look toward the right edge of the road instead of looking ahead. This keeps your vehicle on the road until you pass the other vehicle.

questions.question: You are parking downhill on a two-way road with no curb. Which way should you turn your front wheels?

options.text: Straight ahead
Right, toward the side of the road
Left, toward the center of the road

questions.correctAnswerText: Right, toward the side of the road
questions.explanation: When parking downhill, turn your wheels toward the road edge. Your vehicle will roll away from traffic if the brakes fail. When parking uphill on a road with a curb, turn your wheels toward the center of the road so your vehicle rolls into the curb.

questions.question: If a tire blows out, you should:

options.text: Press the brake and hold it.
Hold the steering wheel tight and use the brakes gently.
Pull over quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hold the steering wheel tight and use the brakes gently.
questions.explanation: Hold the steering wheel tight and keep the car going straight. Lift your foot off the gas pedal slowly and use the brakes gently. Do not stop on the road. Pull off safely when you can.

questions.question: To avoid hydroplaning in rain, you should:

options.text: Drive at normal speed.
Apply your brakes as soon as your car starts to skid.
Slow down.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down.
questions.explanation: Hydroplaning happens when you drive too fast in wet conditions. Your tires lose contact with the road and ride on top of the water. Slow down in rain to keep your tires on the road.

questions.question: Which road surface freezes first?

options.text: A tunnel
An intersection
A bridge

questions.correctAnswerText: A bridge
questions.explanation: Bridges freeze before the rest of the road and thaw after. Pavement on bridges becomes icy even when other areas are dry.

questions.question: When parallel parking downhill, what should you do with your wheels?

options.text: Turn them sharply toward the side of the road.
Turn them away from the side of the road.
Keep them straight.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn them sharply toward the side of the road.
questions.explanation: When parking downhill, turn your wheels toward the curb or road edge. When parking uphill without a curb, turn toward the edge. When parking uphill with a curb, turn away from the curb.

questions.question: If your car begins to skid out of control, you should:

options.text: Pump the brakes.
Apply the brakes gently.
Stay off the brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay off the brakes.
questions.explanation: If your vehicle skids, do not use the brakes. Keep steering until the vehicle is under control and moving safely again.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: Cars in the right lane must slow down.
No left turn.
Merge.

questions.correctAnswerText: Merge.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. This sign warns that traffic is merging from the right. Be ready to let other traffic merge safely.

questions.question: For drivers 21 and older, you are driving under the influence at a blood alcohol concentration (BAC) of:

options.text: 0.02 percent.
0.04 percent.
0.08 percent.

questions.correctAnswerText: 0.08 percent.
questions.explanation: A BAC of 0.08 percent or higher is considered driving under the influence. Alcohol-related convictions can result in fines, jail time, or both.

questions.question: If your tires feel like they have lost contact with the road, you should:

options.text: Slow down by shifting into a lower gear.
Ease your foot off the gas pedal.
Slow down by pumping the brakes quickly and firmly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ease your foot off the gas pedal.
questions.explanation: Ease off the gas pedal and stay off the brakes. Do not stop or turn until your tires grip the road again.

questions.question: At a "Yield" sign, you must:

options.text: Yield to cross traffic that is close enough to cause a conflict.
Yield only to vehicles on your right.
Always slow down and go without stopping.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yield to cross traffic that is close enough to cause a conflict.
questions.explanation: At a yield sign, slow down or stop if needed. Give the right-of-way to any vehicles close enough to cause a conflict.

questions.question: When passing, when should you move back into the right lane?

options.text: When you are one vehicle length ahead.
When you can see both headlights of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.
When you are 50 feet ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you can see both headlights of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.
questions.explanation: Return to the driving lane only when you have enough space. When you can see both headlights of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror, it is safe to return.

questions.question: At an uncontrolled intersection when you arrive at the same time as vehicles to your right and left, you should:

options.text: Yield to the vehicle on your left.
Yield to the vehicle on your right.
Wait until there are no vehicles before proceeding.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yield to the vehicle on your right.
questions.explanation: The vehicle on your right has the right-of-way at an uncontrolled intersection. Drivers then proceed in the order they arrived.

questions.question: Unless otherwise posted, what is the speed limit in an urban district?

options.text: 20 mph.
30 mph.
45 mph.

questions.correctAnswerText: 30 mph.
questions.explanation: The speed limit in an urban district is 30 miles per hour unless a different speed limit is posted. Follow posted speed limits.

questions.question: If you are about to be hit from behind, you should NOT:

options.text: Release your seat belt.
Brace yourself.
Press your head against the headrest.

questions.correctAnswerText: Release your seat belt.
questions.explanation: Keep your seat belt on. Brace yourself by pressing against the back of your seat and put your head against the headrest to prevent whiplash. Hold the steering wheel firmly and be ready to brake.
